claim.quote: This is the first observation of such a long-range, near-side feature in two-particle correlation functions in pp or p p-bar collisions.

date.note: arXiv submission date; published as JHEP 09 (2010) 091

name: Observation of long-range near-side angular correlations in pp collisions ("the ridge")

significance.note: The paper reports a qualitative first observation of the feature and does not quote a statistical significance in the abstract.

summary.plain: In its first year CMS saw pairs of particles flying in the same direction but far apart along the beam, a pattern nobody expected in ordinary proton collisions and previously seen only in collisions of heavy nuclei.
summary.technical: Two-particle Delta(eta)-Delta(phi) correlations in 7 TeV pp collisions show a pronounced near-side ridge at 2.0 < |Delta(eta)| < 4.8 for 1-3 GeV/c tracks in high-multiplicity events (980 nb^-1).

title: Observation of Long-Range Near-Side Angular Correlations in Proton-Proton Collisions at the LHC
why_it_matters: The ridge is a signature previously associated with the quark-gluon plasma; seeing it in proton-proton collisions raised the question of whether collective behaviour also arises in the smallest collision systems.
